title: Cleaning and oiling the clarinet
summary: Hall swabs with chamois every night and sometimes oils the instrument.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: One other question, we started jumping around because I'm just about to run out now. Anyway, I just want you to get a couple more minutes to help us.
That's anything you want, I've got plenty of time.
Anyway, I was wondering about the caravan instrument. Do you ever do any oiling or swapping it when you get through, or what do you advise?
I clean my cabinet every night. Every time I get through clean, I dry it out. Just dry it up the swab? Yeah, I swap it out every night.
Use an ordinary swab, or run it right through it?
No, I have a piece of chamois. Chamois, yeah. Because that absorbs the moisture.
Ever run oil through it or anything?
Sometimes I do. From the inside, the lower too? Yeah, yeah. You can't put too much in it because it'll affect the pads.
